receipt.public_excerpt: “They’re kind of hitting the same ceiling on capabilities. Now there’s lots of smart people in the industry working to break through those ceilings

evidence_items.explanation: Andreessen said frontier LLMs were hitting a shared capability ceiling, with 'a local topping out'. That matches a prediction of diminishing returns.

receipt.public_excerpt: Pichai said “I think the progress is going to get harder,” adding “you’re definitely going to need deeper breakthroughs as we get to the next stage.”

evidence_items.explanation: Pichai said progress would get harder and would need deeper breakthroughs. That fits Marcus's view that current methods face diminishing returns and need new ideas.

receipt.public_excerpt: these are not physical laws. They are just empirical observations that held true, much like how Moore’s Law did for a long time

evidence_items.explanation: Nadella said scaling laws are empirical observations like Moore's law, not physical laws. This nearly repeats Marcus's 2022 wording. The page shows no publication date, so available_at is approximate (Ignite 2024 began 2024-11-19).

receipt.public_excerpt: He also discussed OpenAI’s new scaling law, which focuses on test-time computing

evidence_items.explanation: In the same talk, Nadella pointed to a new scaling path (test-time compute). That partly cuts against reading his remarks as conceding that scaling has hit a wall.

evidence_items.locator: section on scaling, after Kaplan scaling laws discussion

receipt.public_excerpt: Indeed, we may already be running into scaling limits in deep learning, perhaps already approaching a point of diminishing returns.

evidence_items.explanation: Establishes what Marcus predicted in 2022: diminishing returns from scaling. This is the speaker's own writing, used only to fix the baseline being compared, not as proof he was right.
